# Start Here: Infantry First Aid
You're not a medic, but you will get shot. This guide covers everything in your [bold]IFAK[/bold] (infantry first aid kit) and how to use it to keep yourself and your squad alive until a medic arrives. Everything in it works without any medical training.
## What's in Your IFAK
- [bold]Tourniquet[/bold]: stops a bleeding arm or leg. Quick enough to put on yourself under fire. - [bold]Hemostatic gauze packet[/bold]: use the packet in your hand to open it, then use the gauze on a wound. It dresses one wound, then it's gone. - [bold]Ointment[/bold]: treats burns. Use it on a burned body part; a tube has 10 uses. - [bold]Splint[/bold]: holds a broken arm or leg together so moving on it doesn't make it worse. - [bold]First-aid autoinjector[/bold]: a single shot of tricordrazine, which heals all damage a little, and dexalin, which helps with suffocation. - [bold]Tricordrazine pill packet[/bold]: four pills that each heal all damage a little. Don't take more than 2 in a short time. - [bold]Tramadol pill packet[/bold]: four painkillers. Take one at a time, and don't take another for a while. - [bold]CPR mask[/bold]: put it on an unconscious squadmate to make your CPR count for more.
## Using Your Kit - To treat yourself, hold the item and click yourself. To treat someone else, hold it and click them. - To take a pill, open the packet and take a pill out, then use it in your hand to swallow it, or click someone to feed it to them. - Right-click someone and choose [bold]Inspect injuries[/bold] to see their wounds and how badly they're bleeding.
## When You Get Hit Work through these in order.
### 1. Get Out of the Fire Nothing else matters if you keep getting shot. Get into cover first.
### 2. Stop the Heavy Bleeding - Bleeding kills fastest. [color=red]Arterial bleeding[/color] (spurting blood) can drain you in moments. - Bleeding from an [bold]arm or leg[/bold]: put the tourniquet on it. - [bold]Lost a limb[/bold]: the stump bleeds arterially until a medic closes it with surgery. Aim at the missing limb and put the tourniquet on the stump. - [color=red]A tourniquet kills the limb after 5 minutes.[/color] It's there to keep you alive until a medic can treat the wound properly and take it off. Get to a medic, or have your squad call for one.
### 3. Dress the Wounds - Use your hemostatic gauze on your worst wounds. Every open wound bleeds, and untreated wounds stop that body part healing. - You only have two, so save them for wounds that matter.
### 4. Splint Broken Limbs - If an arm or leg is broken, splint it. Moving on an unsupported fracture hurts and makes it worse. - A splint doesn't heal the bone. A medic needs to put a cast on or operate.
### 5. Deal with the Pain - Pain slows you down, throws off your aim and can put you into shock, where you keep collapsing. - Take [bold]one[/bold] tramadol pill. It masks the pain but doesn't fix what's causing it. - Overdosing on painkillers is dangerous. Don't stack them.
### 6. Top Up Your Health - Use the first-aid autoinjector, or take a tricordrazine pill, to heal a little of everything. - These won't fix serious injuries; they just buy time.
## When a Squadmate Goes Down - [bold]Return fire and neutralize the threat first.[/bold] Don't stop to treat anyone while you're still being shot at, unless others are covering you. A second casualty helps no one. - [bold]Call for a medic[/bold]. Give your location. - [bold]Stop their bleeding[/bold] with your own tourniquet and gauze if they're bleeding out. - [bold]Unconscious but alive[/bold]: roll them into the [bold]recovery position[/bold] (right-click them). It helps them breathe while you wait. - [bold]Arterial bleeding and stumps keep bleeding after death.[/bold] Get a tourniquet on them even if they're already dead, or there'll be no blood left by the time a medic arrives. - [bold]Dead[/bold]: they can still be brought back for a while. Put your CPR mask on them and do [bold]CPR[/bold] by clicking them with an empty hand. Each round buys them more time until a medic with a defibrillator arrives.
## Leave It to the Medics Your IFAK keeps people alive; it doesn't fix them. A medic is needed for: - taking off a tourniquet safely - casting or operating on broken bones - internal bleeding, which you can't see or dress - damaged organs - bringing back the dead with a defibrillator
## Restocking Your IFAK pouch can also hold gauze, trauma kits, burn kits, ointment, pills, autoinjectors, splints, blood packs and a CPR mask. Grab spares when you can.
